scope: Optional deeper units; not part of existing 740 topic IDs or the first 28 daily sessions.

units.title: Agent frameworks and contracts

topics.title: Rebuild an observation/tool/result loop in plain Python before adding a framework.
Compare tool schemas, state, persistence, retries, streaming and termination.
Run identical mocked-tool tasks in LangGraph and one contrasting framework.
Compare Python and TypeScript ecosystems; distinguish framework, service and model provider.
Check license, release/version, provider assumptions, telemetry and self-hosting.
Measure overhead, recoverability and testability rather than counting integrations.

units.assessment: one baseline plus two implementations, fixed tasks, traces and a decision record. See [framework comparison](16-agent-frameworks-and-protocols.md).

units.title: MCP, skills and plugins

topics.title: Host/client/server boundaries, discovery and capability negotiation.
Tools versus resources versus prompts; JSON Schema and structured errors.
stdio versus HTTP transport; lifecycle, cancellation and reconnection.
Authentication versus authorization; scoped credentials and user consent.
Version pinning, schema changes and backward compatibility.
Tool-output injection, untrusted metadata and permission checks outside the LLM.
Plugin packaging and skill instructions are host-specific; loading text grants no authority.
A2A peer-agent contracts versus MCP tool/service connectivity.

units.assessment: read-only corpus MCP server with malformed-input, denied-access, disconnect and injection tests. Then add one reversible action behind explicit authorization. [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/getting-started/intro), [A2A](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/).

units.title: Agent swarms and coordination

topics.title: Supervisor/worker, handoff, parallel fan-out and shared blackboard patterns.
Independent work versus dependencies; async execution and backpressure.
Shared memory consistency, provenance, duplicate actions and idempotency.
Message/context budgets, noisy coordination and cascading errors.
Worker failure, timeout, cancellation and bounded recovery.
A single capable agent versus several specialists at equal total budget.
Measure speed, success, cost and unwanted actions; stop when delegation hurts.

units.assessment: single-agent and three-worker research systems tested on the same unseen tasks. A swarm is an orchestration pattern, not proof of intelligence.

units.title: Harness internals and benchmarks

topics.title: Model adapter, context builder, tool executor and event loop boundaries.
Filesystem, shell, patching, Git/worktrees and deterministic verification.
Sandbox, secrets, network permissions and irreversible-action gates.
Resume, checkpoint, compaction and evidence lost through summaries.
Trace one source-code execution path and record the pinned commit.
Pick a task-family benchmark and inspect dataset, environment and grader.
Hold model fixed while changing harness; hold harness fixed while changing model.
Equal budgets, multiple seeds, paired comparisons and contamination controls.
UI exposes capabilities; source/traces show actual behavior. Evaluate both later.

units.assessment: source reading notes and reproducible baseline/ablation table. See [benchmark and harness guide](17-benchmarks-costs-and-harness-study.md).

units.title: LLM economics and LLMOps

topics.title: Input/output/cached tokens, tool calls, retries and reasoning-token billing where exposed.
Costs per request, successful task and active user; report failure spend.
Budget reservations, parallel overspend, time/step limits and cancellation.
Cache invalidation, batching, routing, context trimming and fallback quality.
API versus self-hosting: GPU utilization, idle time, storage and operations.
TTFT, per-token latency, end-to-end p95 and queue delay.
Version prompts, tools, corpus, model and evaluation; canary and rollback.
Drift/quality slices, privacy-redacted traces and incident response.

units.assessment: ledger, fixed-budget experiment and rollback drill; never optimize only token price while ignoring success.

units.title: Open-weight model architecture

topics.title: Model card, license, tokenizer, config, tensors and reference implementation.
Embedding/attention/MLP/norm/residual paths; trace dimensions manually.
Dense versus MoE; total versus active parameters, routing and load balance.
Positional encoding, attention variants and KV memory calculation.
Base/instruct/reasoning/distilled checkpoints and chat templates.
Distinguish architecture, pretraining corpus, post-training recipe and runtime.
Implement one block at toy scale and compare outputs with a reference.
Inspect unavailable data/weights/training details; open weights do not imply reproducible training.

units.assessment: architecture walkthrough of a pinned small model and one toy reproduction. Start with [Qwen3](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3), then study [DeepSeek-V3](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3) and [DeepSeek-R1](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1) as different architecture/post-training examples. These are study examples, not claims about today's best model.

units.title: RAG, cache and memory experiments

topics.title: Corpus knowledge versus user/session memory; provenance, TTL and deletion.
Retrieval, long-context prompting and KV/prefix caching have different roles.
Cold/warm cache, cache invalidation and stale facts after corpus updates.
Bounded versus growing corpus; context limits and distractor sensitivity.
Memory extraction/write/read policies and erroneous remembered facts.
Compare citation correctness, answer accuracy, leakage, latency and cost.

units.assessment: Compare retrieval, cache and memory on fixed queries, updates and cold-start cost.

units.title: Paper reproduction and purposeful product

topics.title: Separate a paper's contribution from a framework's current features.
Reproduce a reduced-scale baseline and one ablation with a held-out split.
Write down data limitations, compute budget and failed attempts.
Identify a user and recurring workflow; compare with an ordinary scripted solution.
Validate usability, quality, permissions and maintenance with actual users.
Publish evidence and limitations, not an employment guarantee.

units.assessment: a technical report plus a small user-tested tool. Choose one project from [the project review](18-final-year-projects-reviewed.md), not twenty simultaneous projects.
